title: What single movement does each set of presses make?
description: Four sets of button presses are joined into one movement each. The floors up and the floors down are totalled and cancelled, and one set is checked from the ground floor.
teaching_notes: One idea: several presses combine into one movement, with floors up and floors down cancelling. Watch for students who add the numbers and ignore the minus signs.

video_script.why: The child combines several button presses into one movement by cancelling the floors up against the floors down.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four sets of presses read as one combined movement
video_script.anchor: the lift in {{NAME_10}}, with sets of two or three presses in a row
video_script.payoff_line: Ups and downs cancel to one single movement.

final_answer.spoken: the single movements are plus five, plus five, minus one and minus two

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: a total of nine for the third and fourth sets
maths_rules: Check c from the ground floor: +4, +1, −1.
video_script.design: One idea: combine presses by cancelling floors up against floors down. One lift picture throughout. Method as in the solved example.

beats.on_screen: title card One Single Movement; the lift panel appears with four sets of button presses listed

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift panel appears
marks.sets: the four sets of presses are listed in the anchor band
marks.ask: the question is written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='sets'/>Four sets of button presses are given, with two or three presses in a row.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Each set makes one single movement. What is it?

beats.on_screen: the four sets stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the lift beside a floor line; presses in a row are joined by a bracket into one arrow; floors up and floors down are drawn as opposite arrows

marks.one: two presses are joined by a bracket into one arrow
marks.way: the solved example from the book is shown beside the lift
marks.cancel: an up arrow and a down arrow are drawn against each other

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Presses in a row can be joined into one movement.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>Floors up and floors down work against each other, so they cancel.

marks.given: the line Given is written with the four sets

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four sets of presses.
The first two sets have only plus presses. The last two sets have plus and minus presses.

beats.on_screen: To find: the single movement of each set

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the single movement of each set.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: all presses go up: (+1) + (+4) = +5 and (+4) + (+1) = +5

marks.up: the first two sets are circled
marks.five: the two arrows join into one arrow of five floors up

narration: <bookmark mark='up'/>Step one, in the first two sets every press goes up.
<bookmark mark='five'/>One floor and four floors make five floors up, in either order.
The single movement is plus five in both.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: (+4) + (−3) + (−2): floors up 4, floors down 3 + 2 = 5, so 4 up and 5 down is 1 down: −1

marks.ups: the third set is circled and the up arrow of four floors is drawn
marks.downs: the down arrows of three floors and two floors are joined into five floors
marks.net: the up arrow and the down arrow cancel to one floor down

narration: <bookmark mark='ups'/>Step two, the third set is plus four, minus three and minus two.
<bookmark mark='downs'/>The floors up total four. The floors down total five, from three and two.
<bookmark mark='net'/>Four up and five down leaves one floor down, which is minus one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: (−1) + (+2) + (−3): floors up 2, floors down 1 + 3 = 4, so 2 up and 4 down is 2 down: −2

marks.ups2: the fourth set is circled and the up arrow of two floors is drawn
marks.net2: the up arrow and the down arrow cancel to two floors down

narration: <bookmark mark='ups2'/>Step three, the fourth set is minus one, plus two and minus three.
The floors up total two. The floors down total four, from one and three.
<bookmark mark='net2'/>Two up and four down leaves two floors down, which is minus two.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the third set from the ground floor: +4, then +1, then −1

marks.check: the lift starts at the ground floor
marks.path: the lift rises to plus four, drops to plus one and drops to minus one

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the third set from the ground floor.
<bookmark mark='path'/>The lift goes to plus four, then to plus one, and then to minus one.
That matches the single movement of minus one.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.pay: the four single arrows are shown together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The single movements are plus five, plus five, minus one and minus two.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Ups and downs cancel to one single movement.
